haiku-low.q1: 401 Unauthorized. Redis is never called, so no rate-limit counter is touched.
haiku-low.q2: One shared budget: all keys map to one customer ID, so the total is the plan limit, 100 per minute for Standard.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After in seconds. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A denied check adds nothing to the counter, so 429s use no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The request was counted when allowed, so the budget stays used even though the backend returned 500.
haiku-low.q6: The request is forwarded (fail open), ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and no X-RateLimit-* headers are added.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is NOT STATED; the limit is open, to be set by Product before launch.
haiku-low.q8: Shared Redis, key rl:{customerId}:{windowNumber}. Keys expire after a 120 s TTL, which removes old counts.
haiku-low.q9: The count resets at each minute boundary, since the window is a fixed one-minute slice of the wall clock.
haiku-low.q10: Redis runs the Lua check-and-increment script one at a time, so concurrent requests cannot overshoot the limit.
haiku-low.q11: The Lua script computes whole seconds until the next window starts, rounded up, giving a value from 1 to 60.
haiku-low.q12: No retries and no local fallback counter. The client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit-* headers.

sonnet.q1: The gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. Redis is never called, so no counter is affected.
sonnet.q2: All three keys resolve to one customer ID and share one budget, so the total is the plan limit (Standard 100 per minute). The Enterprise limit is not set yet.
sonnet.q3: The client gets 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header in seconds. The backend never sees the request because it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. A denied check adds nothing to the counter, so a 429 uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The request was counted when the check allowed it, and the budget stays used even if the backend fails.
sonnet.q6: The gateway fails open and forwards the request to the backend. It emits ratelimit_store_unavailable and adds no X-RateLimit-* headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is OPEN, to be set by Product. Until it is set, Enterprise requests skip the check.
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis, under the key rl:{customerId}:{windowNumber}. The key TTL of 120 s removes old counts.
sonnet.q9: At the next one-minute window boundary. The window number changes, so a new counter key starts from zero. Fixed windows follow the wall clock, using Redis TIME.
sonnet.q10: A Lua script does the check and increment atomically in Redis. Redis runs scripts one at a time, so concurrent requests from different instances cannot overshoot.
sonnet.q11: The Lua script computes it as the whole seconds until the next window starts, rounded up, in the range 1 to 60.
sonnet.q12: No retries and no local fallback counter. The client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit-* headers, so it gets no rate-limit information.
